texts: Calculus is the art of the infinitely small. $(item)Infinitesimals$() come from the reals. With a $(item)Function Graph$() they become $(item)Derivative$() and $(item)Integral Operators$() - rates of change and sums of slices.
Together those make $(item)Differential Manifolds$() - curved spaces smooth enough to do calculus on. They are the stage relativity is written on.

Complex analysis gives $(item)Fourier Series$() (any wave as a sum of pure tones) and $(item)Fractal Sets$().$(br2)Number theory needs $(item)Prime Shards$() - mined in the Platonic Realm, or sieved slowly from naturals - for $(item)Modular Forms$() and the $(item)Riemann Zeta Crystal$(). Riemann's zeros still guard the primes.
Calculus in a box: limits, derivatives, integrals, series and the analytic continuation of functions into the complex plane.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
Analytic continuation is the strangest of these: a function known on a small patch extends in exactly one way across the complex plane. That is how zeta gets a value where its series diverges.
Day 63. The Platonic Realm is self-similar: big islands low down, smaller ones above them, smaller still at the top. Its landmarks are mathematical objects built exactly to their definitions.

Landmarks I have charted:$(li)$(thing)Menger sponges$() with Euclid's Vault at their heart$(li)$(thing)Sierpinski tetrahedra$()$(li)$(thing)Mandelbulbs$()$(li)$(thing)Cantor dust$()$(li)$(thing)recursive trees$()$(li)the $(thing)Hilbert Archive$(), a corridor that walks a Hilbert curve to its treasure.

Two natives guard it. The $(thing)Fractal Wyrm$(), a serpent made of smaller copies of itself. And the $(thing)Axiom Sentinel$(), an icosahedron that spends two seconds proving you wrong - break its line of sight. I learned that the hard way.

Start from nothing - literally. Start from $(item)Axiom Schemas$() and the $(item)Empty Set$() (Void Essence, or plenty of Void Lattice). Von Neumann built every number out of empty sets nested inside each other; I am doing the same.
Proofs, $(item)Power Sets$(), $(item)Aleph-Null$(), the $(item)Continuum$() and the $(item)Axiom of Choice$() follow. Choice is what Banach and Tarski needed to double a sphere.

Category theory sits on top: $(item)Category Lattices$(), $(item)Functor Bridges$() and finally the $(item)Topos$() - a universe of mathematics with its own logic. Category theory studies not things, but the arrows between them.

math_overview.title: The Road to Infinity
texts: Day 1 of the mathematics. Absolute Infinity is no longer a shortcut. To build it I have to build mathematics itself, one branch at a time.

The branches: $(thing)numbers$(), $(thing)analysis$(), $(thing)number theory$(), $(thing)topology$(), $(thing)logic$(), $(thing)sets$() and $(thing)categories$() - each with its own machine and its own symbols.

The $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$() builds number systems, the $(item)Analytic Continuator$() does calculus and analysis, the $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$() does logic, set theory and category theory, and the $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$() takes it all to infinity.
Finally, whole stacks of every branch are compressed into a $(item)Mathematics Singularity$(), which - with Surreal Numbers, Toposes and Continuum Shards - becomes $(item)Absolute Infinity$().

Each number system is built from the one before it. Every step patches a hole: you cannot subtract 5 from 3 in the naturals, or halve 1 in the integers, or square-root 2 in the rationals. So each time, I build something bigger.

$(li)$(item)ℕ$() from qubits and quartz$(li)$(item)ℤ$() adds negatives (antimatter)$(li)$(item)ℚ$() adds division (Casimir plates)$(li)$(item)ℝ$() fills the gaps - with $(item)Transcendental Crystals$() from the Platonic Realm$(li)$(item)i$() from a tachyon's imaginary mass

$(li)$(item)ℂ$() = ℝ + iℝ$(li)$(item)Quaternions$() and $(item)octonions$() give up commutativity, then associativity$(li)$(item)Surreal Numbers$() hold all of them, and every infinity.$(br2)Each step up costs a rule. The surreals cost none and hold everything. Conway called them the largest field.
Counts past infinity: takes a limit, adds one, and keeps going - omega, omega plus one, omega times two, omega squared, epsilon-naught...$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.

Builds the ordinals from $(item)Ordinal Shards$() mined in the $(thing)Transfinite Hierarchy$(): omega, epsilon-naught, omega-one - and the cardinals from them: aleph-one and the inaccessible cardinal that Absolute Infinity needs.
Note: ordinals measure order (first, second... omega-th), cardinals measure size. Omega plus one is a longer line than omega, yet no bigger - both are aleph-null. Infinity is unkind to intuition.
Builds number systems the way mathematicians did: zero, then "the next one", then negatives, fractions, reals and beyond.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

Peano needed only zero and 'successor' to define all of arithmetic. So I begin with $(item)Natural Number Lattices$(). Antimatter gives you negatives ($(item)Integer Ring$()), Casimir plates divide ($(item)Rational Field$()). For the reals you need $(item)Transcendental Crystals$() from the Platonic Realm.
Mathematical objects have to exist somewhere. The $(item)Platonic Compass$() takes you there: a bright realm of floating axiom stone where the five Platonic solids hang in the sky.

Plato held that perfect forms exist apart from the world. Here they do. $(item)Prime Number Ore$(), $(item)Transcendental Ore$() (π and e) and $(item)Fractal Ore$() grow here. Each solid is hollow, with $(thing)Euclid's Vault$() at its exact centre. There are only five such solids - Euclid proved it.
Checks proofs one axiom at a time. Logic, set theory and category theory are all built here.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
Like real proof checkers, it trusts nothing it has not derived. Tedious, but every result it accepts is certain. I made three errors today; it caught all three.
Infinity comes in kinds. The $(item)Cantor Key$() opens a dimension built in strata - each layer of islands higher and sparser than the last - where the ordinals and cardinals are mined.

$(item)Ordinal Shards$() become $(item)Omega$(), $(item)Epsilon-Naught$() and $(item)Omega-One$() in the $(item)Ordinal Recursor$(); $(item)Cardinal Shards$() become $(item)Aleph-One$() and the $(item)Inaccessible Cardinal$() that Absolute Infinity now needs - a size no lesser infinity can ever reach.

Higher dimensions live here too: $(item)Hypersphere Fragments$() make the $(item)Hopf Fibration$(), the $(item)Penteract$() and the $(item)E8 Lattice$(). Look for $(thing)Hilbert's Hotel$(), $(thing)Ordinal Spires$(), $(thing)Tesseract Frames$() and $(thing)Hopf Rings$().

Natives: $(thing)Hilbert Bellhops$() (harmless; they carry the hotel's keys), $(thing)Hypercube Drifters$() (harmless) and $(thing)Ordinal Hounds$(), whose bites stack $(thing)Infinite Regress$() - every hit after makes you take more. Run early.
